h1: The 7 Best Printers for Small Businesses of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven printers for small businesses, from mono lasers to ink tank all-in-ones, compared on duplex, feeders and running costs.
summary: The Brother DCP-L2640DW is our top pick for text-heavy offices because it prints, copies and scans with automatic duplex on a monochrome laser. The Brother HL-L3220CDW is the color laser to buy for client-facing material. The HP OfficeJet Pro 8139 covers fax and multi-page scanning, and the Epson EcoTank ET-2400 is the pick for steady color printing at a low running cost.
intro: A small business usually buys a printer on the sticker price and learns its real cost a year later in toner or ink. The cheapest unit is often the most expensive to run, and a color printer used mostly for black text quietly wastes money. Matching the technology to what you actually print is the single biggest saving.

We reviewed seven printers across laser, inkjet and ink tank technology and ranked them on what they do, how they handle documents, and what they cost to keep running. We judged from the listed specifications and the buyer groups each suits, not from any claim of running a print room.

products.name: Brother DCP-L2640DW Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser
products.verdict: A compact mono laser that prints, copies and scans with automatic two-sided output.
products.description:
The DCP-L2640DW is a wireless monochrome laser multifunction with automatic duplex printing plus copy and scan. It fits law offices, accounting firms and other text-heavy service businesses.

It ranks first because most small business paper is black text, and a laser keeps the per-page cost low while the scanner covers daily paperwork. The color HL-L3220CDW below it prints color but cannot copy or scan.

Buy it if your office produces contracts, invoices and letters. The caveat is no color, and it sits in the $200-500 bucket.
products.idealFor: Text-heavy offices like law and accounting.
products.skipIf: You need color output for clients.

products.name: Brother HL-L3220CDW Wireless Color Laser Printer
products.verdict: Professional color pages at up to 19 per minute with duplex and a 250-sheet tray.
products.description:
The HL-L3220CDW is a laser that prints in color at a rated speed of up to 19 ppm, holds 250 sheets in its tray, and flips pages itself for two-sided jobs. Design studios and real estate offices are its natural buyers.

It ranks second because color laser output looks sharp for brochures and listings, but it is print-only, so the DCP-L2640DW's scanning and copying push that model ahead for general offices.

Choose it when printed color is part of your product or pitch. The caveat is that you will need a separate scanner and the $200-500 price tier.
products.idealFor: Studios and agencies printing client-facing color.
products.skipIf: You also need scanning and copying.

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 8139 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet
products.verdict: A color inkjet with an automatic document feeder, fax and duplex.
products.description:
The OfficeJet Pro 8139 is an inkjet that does four jobs, printing, scanning, copying and faxing, and it feeds multi-page originals through a feeder tray and prints on both sides unaided.

It ranks third because its document feeder and fax make it the most complete office tool in the $100-200 bucket. Compared with the Brother lasers, inkjet running costs tend to be higher for heavy text.

Pick it for a general office that still sends the occasional fax and scans multi-page files. The caveat is the ink cost over time.
products.idealFor: Offices that still fax and scan stacks of pages.
products.skipIf: You print mainly black text in volume.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2400 Wireless Cartridge-Free Supertank Printer
products.verdict: A refillable ink tank that suits steady color printing.
products.description:
The ET-2400 swaps cartridges for a refillable ink tank and prints, scans and copies in color over wireless. It targets businesses that print color often.

It ranks fourth because tank economics shine only with steady volume, and it has no document feeder or fax like the HP OfficeJet Pro 8139. For the right volume, though, refills cost far less than cartridges.

Choose it when color printing is regular. The caveat is that if you print rarely, the savings never arrive.
products.skipIf: You print only a few pages a week.

products.name: HP Smart Tank Plus 651 Wireless All-in-One Ink Tank Printer
products.verdict: Ink tank economics with a document feeder, fax and two years of ink supplied.
products.description:
The Smart Tank Plus 651 uses an ink tank system, ships with two years of ink, and adds an automatic document feeder plus fax, scan, copy and print.

It ranks fifth because it combines the low-cost refills of the Epson with the feeder and fax the Epson lacks, but it costs more, in the $200-500 bucket.

Buy it if you want both ink-tank savings and full document handling. The caveat is that the price is high for a basic office.
products.idealFor: Offices wanting ink-tank savings with full features.
products.skipIf: You want the cheapest printer to buy.

products.name: Brother HL-L2405W Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser
products.verdict: A small mono laser that only prints, and does it dependably.
products.description:
The HL-L2405W is a wireless monochrome laser that handles printing only, with mobile printing and a compact chassis.

It ranks sixth because it lacks the scan and copy functions of the DCP-L2640DW, and there is no automatic duplex listed. It is a cheaper way to get text onto paper in the $100-200 bucket.

Choose it if you already own a scanner and want a dedicated print machine. The caveat is that you will need other gear for everything else.
products.skipIf: You want one machine to do everything.

products.name: Epson Workforce WF-2930 Wireless All-in-One Printer
products.verdict: A cheap all-in-one with a feeder, duplex and fax for light use.
products.description:
The WF-2930 packs a feeder tray, two-sided printing, fax, scanning and copying into a color inkjet body that costs $50-100.

It ranks last because cartridges make it costly if volume rises. For a home-based business with occasional printing, though, it offers the most features per dollar here.

Buy it for a very small operation. The caveat is that it is not built for steady office output.

whatMatters.factor: Laser vs inkjet vs ink tank
whatMatters.detail: Lasers print black text cheaply and fast, inkjets handle color and photos with pricier ink, and ink tank models refill cheaply but suit steady volume. Look for the technology word in the title and choose by what you print most.
Two-sided printing halves paper use and looks more professional. It matters for contracts and reports. Check for 'automatic duplex' or 'auto 2-sided' in the specs rather than a manual option.
An automatic document feeder scans or copies multi-page files without you placing each sheet. It saves time on paperwork. Look for 'ADF' or 'automatic document feeder' in the listing.
Some industries still use fax. If you do, check that the model lists it. Printers like the Brother HL-L2405W omit scan and fax entirely.
Cartridges, toner and ink bottles decide long-term spend. A cheap printer with expensive refills costs more over time. Check the supply type and any bundled ink on the listing.

cards.label: Laser
cards.text: The Brother DCP-L2640DW, HL-L3220CDW and HL-L2405W use toner, which holds up well for occasional or steady text.

cards.label: Ink tank
cards.text: The Epson ET-2400 and HP Smart Tank Plus 651 use refillable tanks, cheaper per page for regular color.

howToChoose.note: Most small businesses should default to a laser, the Brother DCP-L2640DW, unless color is central to the work.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A color laser for crisp text and graphics, with a decent tray and duplex.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Brother HL-L3220CDW is a color laser with a 250-sheet tray and automatic duplex, the best fit.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Output is heavy or professional, so the DCP-L2640DW or the HL-L3220CDW pays back in running cost and polish.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You print rarely. The Epson WF-2930 handles light work for less.

faq.q: Is a laser or inkjet better for a small business?
faq.a: A laser such as the Brother DCP-L2640DW suits text-heavy work. An inkjet or ink tank suits color and photos.

faq.q: What is the most common buying mistake?
faq.a: Buying on the sticker price and ignoring toner or ink cost. Over a year, supplies can exceed the printer's price.

faq.q: Is the EcoTank worth it over an inkjet?
faq.a: If you print color regularly, yes, since refills cost far less than cartridges. For low volume the savings do not arrive.

faq.q: How do I connect these to a network?
faq.a: All are wireless. The HP Smart Tank 5101 style models use 2.4GHz only, so check your router before buying.

faq.q: How do I maintain a laser?
faq.a: Replace toner when prompted and keep the paper path clean. Lasers need less upkeep than inkjets that sit idle.

faq.q: Do I still need a fax?
faq.a: Only if your clients require it. The HP OfficeJet Pro 8139 and Epson WF-2930 include fax; the Brother lasers here do not.

finalTake: The Brother DCP-L2640DW is the best printer for most small businesses because it handles daily text work economically. Buy the HL-L3220CDW when color matters, the HP OfficeJet Pro 8139 when you need fax and a feeder, and the Epson ET-2400 for regular color at a lower ink cost.
